subject: gdistsamp where not all sites surveyed each period.

messages.author: ea7d65e6eb7bf605
messages.subject: gdistsamp where not all sites surveyed each period.
parts:
Hey all,

The dataset I am working with has the following design:
Sites = 315
Primary Periods = 4
Secondary Periods = 2

I am trying to model abundance using gdistsamp but not all of my sites are surveyed each visit.  Some aren't surveyed at all in some years.  This has not a problem when using other model fitting functions (pcount, occu, colext) but all the examples I have seen using distance sampling have had complete survey design.  Anyone have any experience with this?  Thanks in advance.

Paul

parts:
Sorry about that, I forgot to mention I am using gdistsamp() for multiple survey occasions and my question refers to sites that were not surveyed on a certain visit (analagous to an N-mixture situation where you have a different number of repeated visits for some sites).  Your suggestion of padding with 0's applies to sites where a survey was done but no individuals were detected correct?

Maybe most simply my question is whether gdistsamp() requires the same number of surveys for every site.

Thanks

messages.author: d4a835914e61fc5b
messages.subject: Re: gdistsamp where not all sites surveyed each period.
parts:
Hi Paul,

As a follow-up to this (> one year later...), when you used gdistsamp, did padding your data with NAs for the points that were not visited every year (as Andy suggested) end up working?  I am also running gdistsamp for point counts with multiple visits by year (2003-2006), and there are quite a few points that were not visited every year, some 2 times/years, some 3, some 4 (I inherited a "fun" dataset).  When I leave the NAs in the dataset and try to run my null models, I get the following error:

Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) : 
  initial value in 'vmmin' is not finite

However, when I create a "test" dataset by deleting all points with NAs, the models run.  Did you come across any of these problems?

Thank you much,
Sarah
